title: Historical Hits
statementMd:
Hitster is a tabletop game about placing songs into an ordered timeline by guessing their release year. As a longtime member of the Companionless Playing Card Games (CPCG) association, Harper has access to a single-player variant of Hitster. The rules are similar to regular Hitster. Harper starts with an empty timeline. In each round of the game, she draws a card which contains only a QR code on its front. She scans the QR code to listen to the song and afterwards guesses the release year of the song. Afterwards, she turns the card to reveal the song's true release year. Suppose that the true year is $a$ and she guessed $b$. If Harper's timeline does not yet contain a song with a true release year that is strictly between $a$ and $b$, she adds the card to her timeline.$^{\text{∗}}$ Otherwise, she discards the card.

Harper just had a lengthy playthrough of the entire deck of $n$ cards. Despite her thorough knowledge of music, her final timeline is shorter than she expected. Playing a second time now would be boring because Harper remembers the correct year of all the songs, along with her not-so-correct guesses.$^{\text{†}}$ Surely, she was just unlucky with the order in which she drew the cards, she thinks. To confirm her suspicion, Harper turns to probability theory. Suppose that the same cards are presented in an order drawn uniformly at random from the set of all $n!$ permutations. What is the expected length of Harper's final timeline if she repeats her guesses from her last playthrough for all of the $n$ songs?

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/54ae63bbffe1bc3ec82f9af8f5cb656f9b44e134.png)Visualization of a playthrough of the game with the cards of Sample 3 presented in the order of the input. Harper's timeline is shown at the bottom. After the third round, her final timeline contains two cards. The top right of each round shows the back of the card, which Harper cannot see before making her guess.

$^{\text{∗}}$Her guess $b$ never equals another card's true year, so the card's position in the timeline is uniquely determined.

$^{\text{†}}$She developed this incredible memory through many long nights of playing a single-player variant of Memory.

## Input

The input consists of:

- One line with an integer $n$ ($1 \le n \le 3000$), the number of cards.
- $n$ lines, the $i$th of which contains two integers $a_i, b_i$ ($1 \le a_i, b_i \le 10^9$), the correct year and Harper's guessed year for the song of the $i$th card.

It is guaranteed that $a_i \ne a_j$ and $a_i \ne b_j$ for all $i \ne j$.

## Output

Determine the expected length of Harper's timeline if the cards are presented in an order drawn uniformly at random from the set of all $n!$ permutations.

Let $M = 998\,244\,353$. The expected length can be represented as an irreducible fraction $p / q$ where $q$ is not divisible by $M$. Output one integer $p \cdot q^{-1} \bmod M$ (the unique integer $x$ such that $0 \le x \lt M$ and $x \cdot q \equiv p \bmod M$).

## Note

In the first sample, there are two possible orders. If the cards are drawn in the order of the input, then the first card is added to the timeline and the second card is discarded. If the cards are drawn in reverse order, then both cards are added to the timeline. Thus, the expected length is $3/2$. One can verify that $499122178 \cdot 2 \equiv 3 \bmod M$.
statementZhMd:
Hitster 是一款桌游，玩家需要猜测歌曲的发行年份，并据此将歌曲放入按时间排序的时间线中。作为无伴纸牌游戏（CPCG）协会的资深会员，Harper 可以玩到 Hitster 的单人版本。其规则与普通版 Hitster 类似。Harper 最初的时间线为空。每轮游戏中，她抽取一张正面只有一个二维码的卡牌。她扫描二维码聆听歌曲，然后猜测歌曲的发行年份。接着，她翻转卡牌，查看歌曲的真实发行年份。假设真实年份为 $a$，她猜测的年份为 $b$。如果 Harper 的时间线中尚不存在真实发行年份严格介于 $a$ 和 $b$ 之间的歌曲，她就将这张卡牌加入时间线。$^{\text{∗}}$ 否则，她会弃掉这张卡牌。

Harper 刚刚进行了一场漫长的游戏，抽完了整副共 $n$ 张卡牌。尽管她对音乐了如指掌，最终的时间线却比她预想的短。现在再玩一次会很无聊，因为 Harper 记得所有歌曲的正确年份，也记得自己那些不太准确的猜测。$^{\text{†}}$ 她心想，一定只是自己运气不好，抽牌顺序不佳。为了证实自己的猜想，Harper 决定求助于概率论。假设从全部 $n!$ 种排列中等概率随机选取一种顺序，按此顺序呈现同样的这些卡牌。如果 Harper 对全部 $n$ 首歌曲都沿用上次游戏中的猜测，那么她最终时间线长度的期望是多少？

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/54ae63bbffe1bc3ec82f9af8f5cb656f9b44e134.png)按输入顺序呈现样例 3 中的卡牌时，游戏过程如图所示。Harper 的时间线显示在底部。第三轮结束后，她最终的时间线中有两张卡牌。每轮右上角显示的是卡牌背面，Harper 在作出猜测前无法看到它。

$^{\text{∗}}$她猜测的年份 $b$ 不会等于其他卡牌的真实年份，因此这张卡牌在时间线中的位置是唯一确定的。

$^{\text{†}}$她在无数个漫漫长夜里玩单人版记忆配对游戏，练就了这惊人的记忆力。

## 输入格式

输入包括：

- 一行，包含一个整数 $n$（$1 \le n \le 3000$），表示卡牌的数量。
- $n$ 行，其中第 $i$ 行包含两个整数 $a_i, b_i$（$1 \le a_i, b_i \le 10^9$），分别表示第 $i$ 张卡牌上歌曲的正确发行年份和 Harper 猜测的年份。

保证对于所有 $i \ne j$，都有 $a_i \ne a_j$ 且 $a_i \ne b_j$。

## 输出格式

从全部 $n!$ 种排列中等概率随机选取一种顺序，并按此顺序呈现卡牌，求 Harper 最终时间线长度的期望。

令 $M = 998\,244\,353$。期望长度可以表示为最简分数 $p / q$，其中 $q$ 不能被 $M$ 整除。输出一个整数 $p \cdot q^{-1} \bmod M$（即满足 $0 \le x \lt M$ 且 $x \cdot q \equiv p \bmod M$ 的唯一整数 $x$）。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，有两种可能的顺序。如果按输入顺序抽取卡牌，则第一张卡牌会被加入时间线，第二张卡牌会被弃掉。如果按相反顺序抽取卡牌，则两张卡牌都会被加入时间线。因此，期望长度为 $3/2$。可以验证，$499122178 \cdot 2 \equiv 3 \bmod M$。
